title: Partner Butchery Quality and Hygiene Inspection
basis: Azizo internal standard, informed by the Codex Alimentarius General Principles of Food Hygiene, HACCP principles, ISO 22000 and Kenyan food and public-health requirements. It is not a government certificate.
rules: Each item is Pass (100%), Partial (50%), Fail (0%) or Not applicable.
Items carry a weight of 1 to 3; categories carry a weight out of 100.
A failed CRITICAL item caps the total at 59 (grade E) whatever the other scores.
Every Fail needs a written finding. Critical items cannot be Not applicable.

bands.label: Very good
bands.action: Approved. Minor points to fix by the next visit.

bands.label: Satisfactory
bands.action: Approved. Corrective actions due within 30 days.

bands.label: Needs improvement
bands.action: Conditional. Fix within 14 days and re-inspect; consider pausing new orders.

bands.label: Unsatisfactory
bands.action: Suspend the partner until a passing re-inspection.

items.text: Valid county business permit is displayed
Valid public health / food premises certificate is displayed
Medical (food handler) certificates are valid for all staff who handle meat
Licence and owner details match what was declared to Azizo
Meat is bought only from licensed slaughterhouses / suppliers with inspection stamps or documents
Purchase records are kept (supplier, date, quantity)
Meat is received cold, in a clean covered vehicle or container
Fresh appearance: normal colour and smell, no slime or discolouration
Stock is dated and rotated first-in-first-out; nothing past its use-by
Chiller holds meat at 0 to 4 °C (thermometer reading checked)
Freezer holds frozen meat at -18 °C or colder
A temperature log is kept daily
Raw meat is separated from cooked / ready-to-eat food (raw stored below)
Meat is stored off the floor, covered, in clean food-grade containers
No meat is left at room temperature longer than needed
A working thermometer is available
Clean uniforms or aprons are worn and hair is covered
Hands are washed properly; gloves are changed between tasks
No sick staff handle meat, and staff know to report illness
No smoking, eating or spitting in the work area
Cuts and wounds are covered with waterproof dressings
Floors, walls and ceiling are clean, smooth and in good repair
A handwashing station with running water, soap and towels is next to the cutting area
Lighting and ventilation are adequate
Drainage works and there is no standing water
The customer area and display chillers are clean
Toilets are clean and separate from the meat area
Knives, saws, grinders and hooks are cleaned and sanitised after use
Cutting boards and blocks are in good condition and cleaned between raw and ready foods
A cleaning and sanitising schedule is posted and followed
Scales are clean and accurate
Packaging is clean, food-grade and stored covered
No sign of rodents, flies, cockroaches or birds
Pest-control service or measures are in place, with records
Waste, bones and offal are in covered bins and removed daily
Waste is kept well away from meat and packaging
Clean, safe running water is available
Water tanks are covered and cleaned regularly
A separate wash-up area exists
The owner / manager can explain basic food-safety (HACCP) practice
Staff are trained and training is recorded
Complaints and corrective actions are recorded
Findings from the last inspection have been fixed
Prices and weights are honest; no false labelling or false halal claims
